differentiation.occupancy_preservation: This mechanism has no explicit occupancy or entropy regularizer and makes no claim to preserve occupancy by construction. Start with the small declared activation weight; reject any run showing severe code concentration, including a collapse to a handful of level-0 codes, and select only on reproducible downstream Stage-3 recall@10.

vs_r8.why: This uses soft codebook reconstructions to match the observed embedding displacement, rather than contrastive classification over hard L1 code transitions.
It does not train an L1 next-item predictor; the target is the behaviour-linked representation displacement and gradients reach codebook rows.
It does not co-cluster successor profiles with a JS objective; it transports continuous source-target displacement through codebook representations.
It does not solve an entropic OT assignment problem or impose an OT marginal; assignments are per-example soft distances to existing codebook rows.
It has no teacher and no L1-to-three-level distillation objective; it acts on a single affected codebook level through paired residuals.
It does not preserve train-graph diffusion distances; it uses directed observed pair displacement.
It operates in the repository's Euclidean residual/codebook space and does not use hyperbolic gyro-translation.
It computes no hyperbolic Frechet successor barycentres; its codebook representations are soft Euclidean assignments.
It imposes no hyperbolic radial hierarchy or branching objective.
It does not use a Gromov-Wasserstein graph-code matching objective.
Unlike the untouched host, this adds a small behaviour-conditioned term whose differentiable assignment path reaches the codebook, the gradient path not overwritten by the measured host assembly.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: Unlike the gentle behavior_residual_geometry_transport reference arm, this explicitly transports the observed directed residual displacement through soft source and target codebook reconstructions and includes a directed source-alignment component. It does not claim that improved ER implies improved recommendation; downstream Stage-3 recall@10 is the selection criterion, and code-usage collapse is a rejection signature.

equation: For each valid pair b, let p_s[b,j] = softmax_j(-||source[b]-codebook[j]||^2 / tau), p_t[b,j] = softmax_j(-||target[b]-codebook[j]||^2 / tau), q_s[b] = sum_j p_s[b,j] codebook[j], q_t[b] = sum_j p_t[b,j] codebook[j], and y[b] = target[b]-source[b]. Define L = sum_b mask[b] * (|| (q_t[b]-q_s[b])-y[b] ||_2^2 + alpha * (1 - dot(q_s[b], y[b]) / (||q_s[b]||_2 * ||y[b]||_2 + epsilon))) / (sum_b mask[b] + epsilon).
expected_failure_modes: If the host overwrites encoder gradients and the codebook gradient is zero or negligible, trained weights and exported SIDs remain control-identical.
Excessive effective pressure can concentrate assignments into very few codebook rows, sharply reduce code entropy, and degrade downstream recommendation despite a favorable ER.
If the behaviour-linked target pairs are noisy or not predictive of recommendation, the mechanism can alter SIDs without improving Stage-3 recall@10.
If source and target are accidentally exchanged or the directed term is omitted, the swap-source-target metamorphic check will fail.
If masking is ignored or the denominator is wrong, an all-masked batch will produce a nonzero loss or invalid numerical result.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Blocking codebook gradients would repeat the measured host failure in which encoder-only auxiliary gradients are overwritten.
Replacing the differentiable soft assignments with hard assignments blocks the claimed assignment-mediated codebook gradient.
Removing the directed source-alignment component makes the objective invariant to exchanging source and target and violates the declared directionality.
Adding an occupancy-balancing or assignment-pressure objective changes the mechanism and risks repeating the collapse pattern seen with strong codebook assignment pressure.

hypotheses: The transport residual term makes source and target representations jointly organize around codebook rows so that their codebook displacement tracks observed directed behaviour displacement.
The directed source-alignment component distinguishes source from target and adds a behaviour-sensitive signal without using a detached metric.

Selection criterion: retain the mechanism only if matched downstream Stage-3 recall@10 improves over control and the improvement is reproducible across seeds, with no collapse signature in code usage; Hard-L1 ER is diagnostic, not the objective.

symbols.B: Number of source-target pairs in the batch.
symbols.alpha: Weight of the directed source-alignment component within the mechanism.
symbols.codebook[j]: Trainable row j of the codebook used by the affected quantization level.
symbols.mask[b]: Binary validity indicator for pair b.
symbols.p_s[b,j]: Soft assignment probability of source b to codebook row j.
symbols.p_t[b,j]: Soft assignment probability of target b to codebook row j.
symbols.q_s[b]: Soft codebook representation of the source.
symbols.q_t[b]: Soft codebook representation of the target.
symbols.source[b]: Source item residual or representation for pair b.
symbols.target[b]: Behaviour-linked target item residual or representation for pair b.
symbols.y[b]: Observed directed behaviour displacement, target minus source.

tests.statement: On the specified synthetic case, the loss is finite and nonnegative for the supplied valid mask.
Apply the same row permutation to codebook rows; the scalar loss remains unchanged within tolerance.
Exchange source and target while leaving the codebook and mask fixed; the scalar loss changes by more than tolerance.
Set every mask entry to zero; the scalar loss is zero within tolerance.
For the specified synthetic case, gradients with respect to source, target, and codebook are finite; source, target, and codebook gradients are nonzero.

Compare matched auxiliary-off and auxiliary-on host runs. Confirm the codebook receives a nonzero auxiliary gradient after host gradient assembly, then measure code usage, exported hard L1/L2/L3 SIDs, and Stage-3 recall@10; reject if code usage collapses or downstream recall does not improve reproducibly.

title: Behaviour-conditioned codebook directional transport
